chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Nightly broadcasts and the Syndicate behind Ed Fox
summary: The band broadcast nightly; gangsters owned the club until Ed Fox took it.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Seven nights? Was there a broadcast every night?
Every night. Sometimes two, sometimes three times a night.
Did Earl ever say how he got into the Grand Terrace, or -- who was the guy who owned it, Ed Fox?
Ed Fox. Well, the gangsters owned it at first. Ed Fox was the manager.
When you say the gangsters, do you mean the remnants of the Capone mob?
The Syndicate, yeah, the Syndicate. The Syndicate. See, but when the government started cracking up on the books and things, then they just gave it -- they gave the joint to Ed Fox.
Did Capone used to come in there?
Once in a while. When I first started down there, then things got quiet. After they give up the joint --
Yeah. After they give up the joint to Ed Fox, then a few of the small, you know, echelons used to
come in. But it finally died out.
